{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZigfig", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDJRIs", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 75, "title": "Resolve and implement sample-level hidden-envelope semantics for S-DSP bent GAIN", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `d39804fa5ac6fb528b6518cfae0008c37a3f08e4`, each DSP voice stores only committed `env`. Dynamic GAIN arithmetic runs only on eligible rate events, and bent increase selects +32 or +8 using that committed value. There is no separate hidden-envelope state. See [Voice and envelope processing](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/d39804fa5ac6fb528b6518cfae0008c37a3f08e4/crates/snes-core/src/dsp.rs#L174).

The [existing dynamic-GAIN tests](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/d39804fa5ac6fb528b6518cfae0008c37a3f08e4/crates/snes-core/src/dsp.rs#L529) exercise isolated updates above and below the bend, but do not distinguish hidden candidates from committed envelopes during rate holds or live mode changes. [Issue #13's validation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/d39804fa5ac6fb528b6518cfae0008c37a3f08e4/docs/issue-13-validation.md#original-numerical-evidence) explicitly disclaims hidden-envelope correctness.

This is the next incomplete behavior identified by the latest assessment. The supplied open-Issue list is empty; Issue #13 implemented shared rate scheduling, and Issue #73 corrected mixer saturation. Neither completed this behavior.

## Expected outcome

Implement the source-supported distinction between candidate/hidden envelope state and the committed envelope consumed by ENVX and audio, including bent-GAIN decisions during rate holds and transitions into bent GAIN.

### Specification prerequisite and precise contract

Reconcile these hardware-research references before fixing production behavior or numerical expectations:

- [Fullsnes — SNES APU DSP ADSR/Gain Envelope](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm#snesapudspadsrgainenvelope), especially VxGAIN arithmetic and ADSR interactions.
- [Anomie's S-DSP document, jwdonal revision 1212](https://gist.github.com/nyanpasu64/a0d916ce6924912a7116682bf778e9a0#file-apudsp_jwdonal-txt), especially envelope processing, SOUND GENERATION and COUNTERS.
- [Recorded specification attribution and counter convention](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/d39804fa5ac6fb528b6518cfae0008c37a3f08e4/docs/issue-13-validation.md#specification-and-counter-convention).

Repository-only inspection establishes the implementation gap, but does **not** settle the exact hidden-state rules: the external specification text was not accessed during this planning pass. Record the relevant revision, sections and supported operation order in the implementation validation record. An existing test or previous Issue contract is not evidence that a disputed rule is correct.

The working model to resolve is:

1. Begin a non-release envelope evaluation from committed envelope `E`; calculate candidate `T` even when the selected rate will hold `E`.
2. Bent increase uses the preceding hidden state `H` to select the increment around `$600`, rather than substituting current `E`.
3. Determine exactly when `T` replaces `H`, including whether this precedes clamping and occurs at rate zero. Establish the comparison width/signedness, particularly for negative and overflowing candidates.
4. Establish when `clamp(T, 0, $7ff)` becomes committed `E`. Distinguish unconditional direct GAIN and release from rate-controlled ADSR/dynamic GAIN.
5. Establish how ADSR and other GAIN modes populate hidden state before a live switch to bent GAIN, and whether relevant phase transitions precede rate commitment.
6. Establish initialization/retention at key-on, its existing five empty samples, release and the emulator's existing reset paths. Identify unresolved physical reset retention separately.

Replace any contradicted part of this working model with the documented rule and derive expectations again. Implement the resolved sample-level contract; do not merely add a field or retain unsupported requirements to preserve old assertions. Keep the established shared-counter phase unless the reconciliation supplies concrete contrary evidence. This Issue does not claim DSP subcycle timing.

## Context and reproduction

A focused public-register discriminator can avoid BRR/interpolation uncertainty:

1. Configure one NON voice with held rate-zero noise, FLG=`$20`, voice left/right volumes 64, master left/right volumes 64 and direct GAIN=94. KON, consume five empty samples, then sample once: the current model commits `E=1504`.
2. Write bent GAIN=`$e0` and sample once, holding the committed envelope.
3. Write bent GAIN=`$ff` and sample once.

The current code produces `E=1536`, ENVX=96 and stereo PCM `(-6144, -6144)` at step 3, by source arithmetic. Under the working model where step 2 records hidden candidate 1536, step 3 instead commits 1512, giving ENVX=94 and PCM `(-6048, -6048)`. These latter values are a **conditional test design**, not observed hardware results; make them acceptance vectors only after specification reconciliation. Also test the opposite hidden-state branch and sequences with multiple held samples.

Extend the [original uploaded envelope guest](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/d39804fa5ac6fb528b6518cfae0008c37a3f08e4/crates/snes-core/tests/dsp_envelope.rs), whose [MIT provenance is explicit](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/d39804fa5ac6fb528b6518cfae0008c37a3f08e4/tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md#original-envelope-rate-spc700-guest-approved). The [existing APU partition test](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/d39804fa5ac6fb528b6518cfae0008c37a3f08e4/crates/snes-core/src/apu.rs#L840) supplies a suitable comparison pattern.

Scope: the sample-level envelope evaluation/state needed for bent GAIN and its immediate live-mode/lifecycle interactions. No DSP subcycle scheduler, SPC bus-timing rewrite, BRR-directory correction, noise/pitch reconciliation, echo redesign, UI work or enhancement-chip support.

Remaining envelope work must stay explicit: exhaustive ADSR/GAIN transitions and write combinations, physical startup/reset retention, subcycle register sampling and SPC/DSP races are not completed by this Issue.

Inventory scope is unchanged. Partial: `cpu`, `bus`, `scheduler`, `dma`, `hdma`, `controllers`, `ppu-bg`, `ppu-offset`, `ppu-hires`, `ppu-mode7`, `ppu-objects`, `ppu-color`, `ppu-ports`, `ppu-display`, `spc`, `ipl`, `dsp-voices`, `dsp-noise`, `dsp-pitch`, `dsp-envelope`, `dsp-echo`, `dsp-timing`. Unimplemented: `ppu-raster`, `pal`. None is promoted to verified by this plan.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Document and implement the reconciled candidate/hidden/committed operation order, arithmetic, bend comparison and immediate lifecycle rules. Separate specification facts, derived expectations and retained sample-API conventions. Correct contradicted earlier envelope contracts explicitly.
- [ ] Add original independent numerical vectors distinguishing hidden state from committed state: below/at/above `$600`; rate-zero and nonzero holds; consecutive holds; rate-31 commitment; lower/upper clamp cases; direct GAIN and ADSR transitions into bent GAIN. Include release/retrigger/reset isolation checks for the implemented lifecycle. Assert exact envelopes, ENVX and selected OUTX/PCM values. Expectations must not call production envelope helpers or use another emulator's output as the oracle.
- [ ] Include a public-register sequence exposing a source-supported behavioral difference, without seeding private hidden state. Record its failure against the exact baseline and pass with the correction. Do not count an assertion about a newly added private field as the sole baseline failure.
- [ ] Add or extend an original MIT SPC700 guest uploaded through the existing firmware-free protocol. Exercise `$F2/$F3` writes, a live transition exposing the correction and guest-recorded ENVX checkpoints. Use bounded acknowledgements/execution and documented sampling windows; assert numerical audio output with original data. Update provenance. Acquire no commercial ROM or firmware.
- [ ] Compare every PCM sample and all DSP registers between whole and irregularly partitioned APU advancement across the new transitions and a shared-counter wrap. Apply identical writes at identical emulated boundaries. Partition equality supplements numerical assertions; it does not establish physical timing.
- [ ] Pass `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace --locked`. Preserve existing envelope scheduling, noise, pitch, echo, ordered mixing, controller, DMA/HDMA and PPU coverage. Any corrected legacy envelope expectation needs specification-backed justification.
- [ ] Run the [README validation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/d39804fa5ac6fb528b6518cfae0008c37a3f08e4/README.md#validate) and existing CI gates before merge: reproduce `smoke.bin`; build pinned assemblers with `python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc`; run `tools/hardware-tests.py` with the documented ca65/ld65/spcasm paths and `tools/ppu-test.py` with the documented bass path. Retain source pins, licensing decisions and fixture assertions.
- [ ] Rebuild cleared Castle and Memory twice using `python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py`; run `npm --prefix web ci`, `npm --prefix web run build`, install Chromium as documented, then `npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'`. Preserve existing game sources, expected hashes, replay routes, durations, music/effect assertions and mandatory browser coverage.
- [ ] Record commands, actual results, baseline failures and remaining limitations. All mandatory checks must pass before merge. Update README/validation descriptions without implying full hardware accuracy, commercial compatibility or completion of Issue #3. No suites were rerun during this read-only planning pass.

## Optional validation

Additional independently derived envelope sequences, or voluntarily available physical-device captures with explicit provenance. Neither physical-device access nor subjective listening is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
